title: 表面に詰める (Surface Patch Packing) / リングの皮

T16 input/loop consolidation. Build passed; real-coordinate surface click added and selected patch #52, increasing patches 51 to 52 and history 2 to 3. Existing capacity auto-switch to beads preserved.

T11 v0.2 'リングの皮': added Patch.shape (coin/flatRing/ring3d). Coin path is the exact T10 logic factored into buildCoinPoints (behavior unchanged, verified: fresh coin pack still produces the same kind of irregular blob patches). flatRing (buildFlatRingPoints) places ringNodeCount nodes on a tangent-plane circle of radius anchorR*holeRatio with node radius anchorR*(1-holeRatio)*0.9 -- a real hole opens once holeRatio exceeds ~0.47, below that it reads as a coin (仮決め, no principled derivation, documented in README). ring3d (buildRing3dPoints) reuses S-rings' generateRingBalls/rotatePoint (../rings/ring.ts, imported not copied -- T11's '最大限共有'): ring center = anchor + normal*tubeR, axis = normal, giving a torus tangent to the host's local tangent plane along the full circle of radius R (elementary tangency condition, derivation in field.ts doc comment); random phase applied post-generation via rotatePoint since generateRingBalls itself has no phase parameter. generateShapePoints is the shared dispatch used by both packPatchesGreedy and main.ts's manual-add click handler. gap's UI range widened to [-0.3, 0.3] (T11 §2 'パッキング間隔つまみに負側') -- the underlying formula (clearance - gap) was untouched, a negative gap simply enlarges the allowed radius, permitting deliberate overlap so ring tubes can pass through neighboring rings' holes. compositeSdf's plate-mode branch now splits by shape: coin/flatRing patches still intersect with the shell band (T10-identical, verified no regression), but ring3d patches are unioned RAW (never intersected with the shell) because a ring only touches the surface along one circle and would be sliced to a sliver otherwise -- this means 'plate mode + only ring3d patches' automatically satisfies T11 完了条件3 ('ホスト表示 off でも形が立ち上がる') without a separate visibility toggle: verified via screenshot, the host's egg silhouette read purely from a cluster of 111 tangent rings with zero shell geometry drawn. Window mode is unaffected (any shape still just carves the shell). shaders.ts replicates the identical split in GLSL: the existing uPatchData[i].y owner-index uniform slot now also encodes shape via a +0.5 fractional offset (isRingPoint = fract(y) > 0.25) instead of adding a 4th uniform array, since this Study already hit the fragment uniform-vector budget once at T10. New linking.ts instrument reuses rings/linking.ts's gaussLinkingNumber directly (a ring3d patch's points array, in generation order, already IS the closed centerline polyline the function expects) plus a local adjacency heuristic (candidate pairs = closest point-pair clearance within 3x patch size, 仮決め) and union-find for a connected-component count; also findDeepPatchOverlaps (fusion warning, same 0.55 threshold and caveat as rings' findDeepOverlaps, generalized to any two patches not just rings). meshExport.ts's sampling-bounds padding replaced a thickness/2-only heuristic with bounds computed directly from every patch point's actual position+radius (exact, strict superset of the T10 coin-only case) since ring3d patches can extend well past the shell band. UI added: shape selector (3 buttons), ring-specific slider group (RING_SPECS: flatRingHoleRatio/ringNodeCount/ringTubeR/ringWobbleR/ringWobblePos), and a 絡み計器 gauge panel (linked/adjacent pair ratio, component count, overlap warning count). Verified end to end (isolated Chrome port 5185, real PointerEvent clicks after elementFromPoint hit-test + scrollIntoView): coin unregressed (51 patches, shape all 'coin'); flatRing O-shaped windows visible in window-mode screenshot; ring3d with gap=-0.12 packed 111 patches, plate-mode screenshot showed the host's egg silhouette with ZERO shell rendered (完了条件3 confirmed visually); linking gauge on that packing reported 401 adjacent / 58 linked pairs / 63 components (raw Lk values from -5.05 to 3.00, i.e. some multi-wrap links, not just ±1); mesh inspection at resolution 80 gave plate mode 91,376 triangles watertight (0 open/non-manifold edges) but 191 connected components (more than the live gauge's 63 -- an HONEST discrepancy recorded in README, hypothesized cause: individual rings' own nodes can fragment at this resolution/roundK, a NEW failure mode beyond T10's cross-patch fusion gap, left as unresolved in Next) and window mode gave 189,032 triangles watertight with the shell staying in 1 connected piece; history export->import round-tripped byte-for-byte (16 entries, JSON string match modulo exportedAt) including the new shape/negative-gap data. All 7 pre-existing pages (index/gravity/sag/mpm/foam/rings/pack) verified console-error-free (no regression). npm run build passes with the Patch.shape now required, SkinParams' 6 new fields, and UiHandles.setGauges' extended signature.

T10 initial implementation: new Study S-skin. Host = S1 ball list + k (unchanged, imported from cloud-sculpt/field.ts, same as pack). Shell = |hostSdf| - thickness/2 (field.ts's shellSdf). Patch = an anchor point projected onto the host surface via SDF-gradient Newton descent (field.ts's projectToSurface) plus 3-8 sub-points scattered in the anchor's local tangent plane and re-projected, all smooth-min'd together with one roundK -- structurally just another Ball[]-like point list, no new distance math invented (only the placement -- points hugging a curved surface instead of floating in open space -- is new). Multiple patches are one flat union (patchesSdf), mirroring pack's void-field reuse of a single roundness knob for both intra-group blending and the boolean op with the host (仮決め, same precedent). Composite is mode-dependent: plate mode = opSmoothIntersection(shellSdf, patchesSdf, roundK) (殻∩パッチ群), window mode = opSmoothSubtraction(patchesSdf, shellSdf, roundK) (殻−パッチ群) -- both Quilez smooth booleans, written locally in field.ts (not imported from pack, keeping the Study self-contained same as pack did relative to foam). New op packPatches carries the resulting patch list (anchor+sub-points+radii) explicitly, mirroring pack's packVoids/mpm's freeze precedent -- replay never re-runs the greedy walk or the surface projection. New op setMode records the plate/window toggle itself, so mode survives export->import even though it doesn't touch the packing data (completion condition 5 explicitly wants full history reproduction). Manual patch add (click while in add-patch mode, host-only raymarch target, same simplification pack made) places a light 3-point spray rather than running the full irregularity/gap logic -- documented as not honoring gap, same as pack's manual void add. Gauges: estimateMortar (cross-patch point-pair clearance, same dual reading as pack's thinnest-wall proxy -- 'thinnest mortar' in window mode, 'closest two plates came to touching' in plate mode), estimateCoverage (two stacked Monte Carlo approximations: shell-band volume as a proxy for surface area, then patch-membership fraction within that), estimatePatchComponents (a FAST proxy -- union-find over patch-to-patch point proximity, meaningful only for plate-mode 'how many patches fused into how many pieces', explicitly documented as NOT modeling window-mode shell connectivity). The AUTHORITATIVE connected-component count T10 完了条件3 asks for is computed separately, in meshExport.ts's countConnectedComponents, via union-find over the actual generated triangle soup's shared vertices (same vertex-quantization convention as cloud-sculpt's inspectWatertight) -- this is the number the README's completion-condition verification cites, not the live proxy. Mesh export pads the host's own sampling bounds by thickness/2 on every side (the shell band extends that far past the host's raw ball-radius envelope) before delegating to buildMeshFromField. Added nav links to/from all 7 existing pages. Two real bugs found and fixed during isolated-Chrome verification (port 5185), both from the same root cause: the first GLSL draft (768-point uniform arrays for host+patch pos/radius/owner) exceeded MAX_FRAGMENT_UNIFORM_VECTORS(1024) on the verification renderer, fixed by lowering HOST_MAX_BALLS 128->96 and PATCH_MAX_POINTS 768->256 and folding patch radius+owner into one vec2 uniform array (uPatchData) instead of two separate float/int arrays. Second, and more substantive: real-coordinate click verification (AGENTS §3) found that click-to-select silently failed on every plate-mode patch -- picking.ts's 'which patch owns this point' test used a zero-surface-distance threshold (correct for window mode, where only a carved opening's rim belongs to a patch) but plate mode's visible surface is shell∩patches, so almost every rendered plate-face point sits deep inside a patch's point spheres, never near their own zero surface. Fixed by making picking.ts's nearestPatchId (and the equivalent shader onPatch/coloring logic) mode-aware: plate mode picks the nearest patch unconditionally (no threshold), window mode keeps the rim-only threshold test. Verified after the fix: real PointerEvent click selected a plate patch ("選択中: パッチ #38"), real Delete keypress removed it (44->43, removePatch recorded).

Added the full-mesh overlay view (raymarch is capped at ~160 patches/256 points by the uniform budget and silently under-draws dense packings — the author read a fully packed ring skin as sparse). Also authored recipes/ring-cover-20260713.json: 869 rings in two greedy passes fully clothe the host (2,578 interlinked pairs, 31 components).

T12 'skin の生きた表示' (v0.3): two author reports -- (1) flatRing/ring3d selection didn't turn the highlight color despite picking working; (2) raymarch-capacity-limited views weren't interactive enough, mesh-overlay checking was heavy. Investigated report (1) against the suspected root cause in the task brief (owner-index fractional encoding for ring3d, uPatchData[i].y = pi + 0.5, compared against uSelectedPatchOwner) and found shaders.ts's nearestPatchOwner() already floors correctly (int(floor(uPatchData[i].y + 0.01))) -- verified empirically in isolated Chrome (port 5185) that highlighting DOES work correctly for all three shapes when the selected patch's points fall within PATCH_MAX_POINTS (256). The actual root cause: flatRing/ring3d patches have far more points per patch (ringNodeCount~10) than coins (4-9 sub-points), so a typical pack (50-110 patches) blows the 256-point uniform budget almost immediately -- patches beyond the budget are never uploaded to the GLSL uniform arrays at all, so CPU-side picking (picking.ts, unbudgeted) finds and selects them but the GPU-side highlight has no geometry to color, explaining the author's precise phrasing ('picking seems to work, but it doesn't turn color'). Also fixed a second, independently-found bug: clicking a patch-shape button (コイン/平リング/立体リング) recorded the state change but never updated the button's own mode-active CSS class (main.ts's onSkinParamChange callback only called record()+afterMutation(), never ui.ts's renderShapeButtons) -- added a lightweight ui.setPatchShape(shape) called only on patchShape changes (full syncSkinParams, which re-renders every slider, stays reserved for history replay). Built the bead approximation view (renderer.ts's updateBeads/updateBeadSelection/setViewMode): THREE.InstancedMesh spheres for every host ball (translucent backdrop, opacity 0.16) and EVERY patch point with no uniform-array cap, using instanceColor (setColorAt, no geometry rebuild) for the existing cross-Study selection color (vec3(1,0.75,0.2) -- kept instead of inventing a literal blue per AGENTS §5's 'pick one scale and don't change it'; the author's 'turns blue' is read as colloquial for 'gets highlighted'). Picking/manual-add reuse picking.ts's raymarchComposite/raymarchHost unchanged (verified working in bead mode too). main.ts gained a three-way viewMode ('raymarch'|'beads'|'mesh') replacing the old boolean overlayActive, with an auto-switch rule in afterMutation(): once total patch points exceed PATCH_MAX_POINTS while on raymarch, switch to beads and show a one-shot 'auto-switched' banner (ui.ts) -- retiring T11's silent-truncation raymarch-only default, which the task brief explicitly called out as the root of the 'looks sparse' misreading. Mutating state while on 'mesh' drops back to raymarch/beads (mesh-invalidation rule generalized from T11's boolean version). Also gated the raymarch-only capacity warnings in updateSelectionLabel (host/patch/point count caps) behind viewMode==='raymarch' -- showing them in beads/mesh mode would describe a limit that view doesn't actually have (AGENTS §6). Verified end to end: recipes/ring-cover-20260713.json (869 rings, 6,952 points) auto-switches to beads on import and renders as one coherent mass; direct render() benchmarking (window.__skin.benchmarkRender(n), added because the automated verification tab reports document.hidden=true which throttles/pauses the on-screen rAF-based fps counter to ~0) measured ~0.30ms/frame average over 150 calls at that scale -- a CPU-submission-cost lower bound, not a vsync-inclusive real fps; the actual on-screen smoothness on the author's own machine is left as a visual-confirmation item, honestly flagged in README rather than claimed from this measurement. All 8 pre-existing pages verified console-error-free; STL inspect/export, mesh-overlay toggle, and history export/import round-trip all re-verified with no regression. npm run build passes.
